note.explanation: A force can be split into two perpendicular components: one along the x-axis and one along the y-axis. If these components are known, use Pythagoras to find the force’s magnitude and the tangent ratio to find its direction.
examples: If F_x = 3 N and F_y = 4 N, then F = √(3² + 4²) = 5 N.
For the same components, θ = tan⁻¹(4/3) ≈ 53.1°.
note.simple: The x- and y-components are the horizontal and vertical parts of a force. Join them at a right angle: Pythagoras gives the force’s size, and tan⁻¹ gives its angle.
note.checkQuestion: If F_x = 3 N and F_y = 4 N, what are the magnitude and direction of the force measured from the positive x-axis?
note.title: Finding a Force from Its Perpendicular Components
steps: Use F = √(F_x² + F_y²) to find the magnitude.
Use θ = tan⁻¹(F_y/F_x) to find the direction.
State the magnitude in newtons and the angle with its reference direction.

mcqs.stem: Two perpendicular components of a force are 3 N and 4 N. What is the magnitude of the force?
rationales: Correct: F = √(3² + 4²) = 5 N.
Incorrect: 7 N is the sum of the component magnitudes, not their perpendicular resultant.
Incorrect: 12 N is not obtained by applying Pythagoras to the components.
Incorrect: 25 is the squared magnitude, not the magnitude in newtons.

mcqs.stem: A force F makes an angle θ with the horizontal x-axis. Which expression gives its x-component?
rationales: Incorrect: F sin θ gives the y-component for an angle measured from the x-axis.
Correct: The x-component is F_x = F cos θ.
Incorrect: F tan θ is not the expression for either component.
Incorrect: Dividing by cos θ does not give the x-component.

mcqs.stem: A force F makes an angle θ with the horizontal x-axis. Which expression gives its y-component?
rationales: Correct: The y-component is F_y = F sin θ.
Incorrect: F cos θ gives the x-component for an angle measured from the x-axis.
Incorrect: F tan θ is not the expression for the y-component.
Incorrect: Dividing by sin θ does not give the y-component.

mcqs.stem: Which equation gives the magnitude of a force from its perpendicular components?
rationales: Incorrect: Adding the magnitudes directly does not apply the Pythagorean theorem.
Correct: The magnitude is F = √(F_x² + F_y²).
Incorrect: This is the square of the magnitude, not the magnitude itself.
Incorrect: This ratio is not a formula for the magnitude.

mcqs.stem: Which equation gives the angle θ of a force from its perpendicular components?
rationales: Incorrect: This reverses the component ratio and gives the wrong angle.
Incorrect: The section gives the direction using the tangent ratio, not this sine ratio.
Correct: The direction is θ = tan⁻¹(F_y/F_x).
Incorrect: The section does not use this cosine ratio to determine the direction.

mcqs.stem: A 160 N force acts at 60° to the horizontal. What is its x-component? Use cos 60° = 0.5.
rationales: Incorrect: 100 N is not 160 × cos 60°.
Incorrect: 138.6 N is the y-component, found using sin 60°.
Incorrect: 160 N is the whole force, not its x-component.
Correct: F_x = F cos θ = 160 × 0.5 = 80 N.

example.question: A force of 160 N is acting on a wooden box at an angle of 60° with the horizontal direction. Determine the values of its x and y components.

explain.title: A force has two perpendicular components
explain.body: “The magnitude and direction of a force can be found if its perpendicular components are known.” These components are along the x- and y-directions.

explain.title: Find the magnitude
explain.body: “Applying Pythagorean theorem to the right angled triangle OAC (Fig. 4.11-b).” The book gives F² = F_x² + F_y², so F = √(F_x² + F_y²).

explain.title: Find the direction
explain.body: “The direction of F is given by tan θ = F_y/F_x” or θ = tan⁻¹(F_y/F_x). Use a table of trigonometric ratios or a calculator to determine θ.

explain.title: Resolve a force at an angle
explain.body: When θ is measured from the horizontal x-axis, use F_x = F cos θ and F_y = F sin θ. The cosine gives the horizontal part; the sine gives the vertical part.

mistakes: Swapping sine and cosine: with θ measured from the horizontal x-axis, use cosine for F_x and sine for F_y.
Adding perpendicular component magnitudes directly instead of using F = √(F_x² + F_y²).
Forgetting the square root when calculating the magnitude.
Using F_x/F_y instead of F_y/F_x in θ = tan⁻¹(F_y/F_x).
Leaving out units such as N from component answers.
